output:
Short answer
- Look for an LED task lamp with high efficacy (low watts, high lumens), adjustable head/arm, dimming and tunable color temperature (if you need flexible lighting). From the products in your catalog, the “Harbor Task Lamp” is the closest match — I can compare its specs to other options if you want.

Why LED task lamps are the best choice for an energy-efficient office
- LEDs use far less electricity than incandescent/halogen and last much longer, so they reduce both energy use and replacement frequency. (This is a general industry finding; exact savings depend on the lamp wattage and hours of use — verify with product specs and local electricity rates.)
- A good office task lamp focuses light on the work area so you don’t need higher room lighting levels, which reduces total office energy use.

What to look for (specs and features)
- Power and efficacy: target a lamp that uses 5–15 W but delivers 400–1,000 lumens (look for >60–80 lm/W for good efficiency).
- Color temperature: 2700–3500 K for warm, 4000–5000 K for cooler/task lighting. Tunable white is useful if you want both warm and cool lighting.
- CRI (color rendering index): CRI ≥ 90 when accurate color is important (e.g., design work); CRI ≥ 80 is fine for general office tasks.
- Dimming: smooth dimming down to low levels saves energy and increases comfort.
- Beam control & glare reduction: adjustable head, diffuser or louver to avoid glare on screens.
- Mounting options: clamp, weighted base, or hard-mount depending on desk layout.
- Controls & smart features: presence/motion sensors, timers, or smart scheduling save energy by shutting lights off when unused; integrated USB/PD ports add convenience but check their power draw.
- Safety/certifications: ENERGY STAR and DLC (DesignLights Consortium) are strong energy-performance indicators; UL/ETL for safety.

Evidence available and claims that require verification
- Catalog memory shows the entry “Harbor Task Lamp” (and generic “adjustable desk lamps” / “task lamps” / “lighting products” / “desk accessories”). I do not have detailed provenance or spec-sheet text for that Harbor Task Lamp in memory — so any detailed claims about its wattage, lumens, CRI, color-temp range, dimming, ENERGY STAR/DLC listing, or motion sensors must be verified from the product spec sheet or vendor page.
- General claims about LED energy savings (e.g., “LEDs use ~75–85% less energy than incandescent and last 15–25× longer”) are commonly stated by manufacturers and agencies (ENERGY STAR, EPA). You should verify the exact percentage and lifetime claims for any specific lamp with the manufacturer’s spec sheet or third‑party certification.
- If I recommend a specific wattage-to-lumen ratio or expected annual energy savings, those are estimates — they require verification of the lamp’s rated lumens/watts and your actual daily usage and electricity cost. Example: replacing a 60 W incandescent with a 10 W LED saves 50 W while in use; at 8 hours/day that’s ~146 kWh/year saved — multiply by your local kWh cost to get dollars saved.

Concrete next steps I can do for you
- Pull full specs for the Harbor Task Lamp and two other high-efficiency desk lamps from your catalog and compare: watts, lumens, lm/W, CRI, CCT range, dimming, sensors, certifications, mounting, price, and warranty.
- Or if you prefer, give me your priorities (budget, need for tunable white or high CRI, clamp vs base, desire for motion sensors or USB ports) and I’ll recommend 1–2 best-fit models and list exactly which claims need verification and what to check on the spec sheet.

Which would you like me to do next?
